title: Public input on Kitchener's proposed 2023 budget
subtitle: Delegates raised trails, cycling, economic development, physician recruitment, climate programs and cost of living; no motions were made.
overview: The Special Finance and Corporate Services Committee met to hear public input on the proposed 2023 City of Kitchener budget. The committee made no recommendations at this meeting. Under the meeting's rules, delegates spoke and members asked only clarifying questions. Staff were not questioned, and questions are to be raised later in the operating and capital budget reviews and on final budget day.

Six delegates spoke. A resident asked for long-promised trails in the Grand River South community to be funded. Two residents urged more money for cycling infrastructure, and one raised cost-of-living and wage concerns. The Waterloo Region Economic Development Corporation reported on 2022 investment and asked for continued municipal support. The KW Chamber of Commerce asked for continued support for family physician recruitment. Reep Green Solutions reported on climate actions and supported the proposed greener fleet and trail upgrades.
The input will inform the committee's later budget deliberations, where council will set the 2023 property tax increase and spending priorities. The meeting adjourned after the last delegation.
debate: A Grand River South resident asked that off-street trails be added to the 2023 budget. The resident pointed to a decade of City plans and studies showing the trail system, a petition with almost 500 signatures, and the lack of a safe walking route to a local public school beyond busy regional roads.

Two delegates said cycling infrastructure is under-funded compared with road reconstruction. One said it would receive under $2 million in 2023 and less in later years, and suggested the parking enterprise's forecast loss as a possible funding source. A councillor asked about bicycle parking and another about e-scooters. The delegate supported both.

The economic development delegate said Kitchener received a large share of 2022 deals and praised fast building permits. The delegate warned of a global recession, a shortage of shovel-ready sites, and cuts to federal export funding that leave a shortfall in the business development budget. A resident later asked why Cambridge's total investment was similar to Kitchener's. Staff replied that most employment land is in Cambridge and Woolwich Township.

The Chamber of Commerce delegates said the region needs several new family doctors each year just to keep pace with retirements and growth. They also said a large share of local family physicians may retire within five years, and that city funding helps them raise private-sector support.

One delegate said a tax increase below inflation amounts to a service cut. The delegate also argued that some part-time City wages fall below the regional living wage and that salary spending is poorly allocated. Another delegate asked the committee to fund the enhanced green options, including fleet greening and trail upgrades, and said low-income energy efficiency programs are an unmet need.
